description: Sync Attio records and list entries from the objects and lists you choose, with notes, tasks, comments, meetings and call transcripts. Private list access carries over when Enforce ACL is on.
opening: Sync records from the Attio objects you select, such as people, companies and deals, and entries from the lists you select. Notes, tasks, meetings and call transcripts sync for the whole workspace, and comments sync for the selected records and entries. Each item is one document. Notes, tasks, comments and list entries link to the record they belong to, and a transcript links to its meeting.

An entry of a private Attio list can be restricted to the list's admins and directly granted members. Search applies this only when Enforce ACL is on. Object records, notes, tasks, meetings and transcripts carry no Attio restriction. Attio has no last-edited time, so results rank by when an item was created. Items deleted in Attio can stay in HydraDB.

permissions.who_can_read: An entry of a private list, and the comments on it, can be read by workspace admins and the members granted access to the list directly. An entry of a list open to the whole workspace, every object record and the comments on it can be read by everyone who can query the collection, unless you set an access rule. Notes, tasks, meetings and call transcripts do not take on a list's restriction.
permissions.when_unreadable: If HydraDB cannot read a list's settings or members, or the list's readers come out empty or too many, the connector reports a permission warning for that list.
notes: Access granted only through a team cannot be read, so team members without a direct grant cannot read a private list's entries in HydraDB.
Suspended members, and grants to people no longer in the workspace, are left out.
Reading list access needs the `list_configuration:read` and `user_management:read` scopes.

connect.auth: Attio uses a workspace API key. An OAuth access token also works.

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: An Attio workspace API key, from Workspace settings, Developers, API keys, or an OAuth access token.

permissions.name: list_configuration:read
permissions.text: also needed to carry over private list access.

permissions.name: user_management:read
permissions.text: also needed to carry over private list access.

steps.title: Create an API key
steps.text: In Attio, open Workspace settings, Developers, API keys. Create a key with the read scopes above.

steps.title: Select objects and lists
steps.text: HydraDB lists the workspace's objects and lists. Select the ones to sync. Records and entries are read only from what you select. Notes, tasks and meetings are read for the whole workspace, including notes and tasks on records of objects you did not select.

connect.account: One connector reads one Attio workspace.

sync.first_sync: Selected objects and lists are read in full. Notes and tasks reach back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default, by creation time. Meetings are read from that point to 30 days ahead.
sync.changes: By default, each selected object and list is read in full on every sync, and only items whose content changed are updated. Notes and tasks inside the window are read again on every sync. Comments are read through their records and entries, and transcripts through their meetings.
sync.edits: A full read picks up edits. Notes, tasks and meetings outside the window are not read again, so later edits to them do not arrive.
sync.deletes: Items deleted in Attio can stay searchable in HydraDB. Items that fall outside the window stay in HydraDB.
notes: The shortest sync interval for Attio is 15 minutes.
Attio's rate limit is shared with every other integration in your workspace. Reading large objects in full on every sync uses it each time.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_id
shared_attributes.text: On a record, the object's slug. On a list entry, the list's slug. On a note, task or comment, the record or entry it belongs to. Limits a query to one object, one list, or one record's items. Not set on meetings and transcripts. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_name
shared_attributes.text: The readable name of the object, list or parent. Limits a query by that name. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: additional_metadata.container_type
shared_attributes.text: What the item hangs off: `attio_object` for records, `attio_list` for list entries, or the parent kind for notes, tasks and comments. Not searchable.

shared_attributes.name: connector_id
shared_attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

documents.name: People and companies
documents.title: The record's name, full name, title, domain or email. Else its first filled-in attribute. Otherwise a title with the object and record id.
documents.text: A header naming the object and record, then each attribute as a labeled line, in alphabetical order. An attribute with several values shows only its first current value, except emails and phones, which are all kept. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the record was created in Attio.
documents.link_back: The record in the Attio web app.

attributes.name: display_name
attributes.text: The record's name. For a person, the graph treats the record as that person.

attributes.name: entity_type
attributes.text: Person for the people object, organization for companies. Decides whether the record stands for a person in the graph.

attributes.name: email
attributes.text: The first current email address. Identifies the person in the graph.

attributes.name: emails
attributes.text: The other current email addresses. Connected to the same person in the graph.

attributes.name: phones
attributes.text: The current phone numbers, written as a `Phones` line.

attributes.name: job_title
attributes.text: The current job title.

attributes.name: handles
attributes.text: The LinkedIn URL and X handle. Can identify the person in the graph.

attributes.name: organization_name
attributes.text: A person's current company name.

attributes.name: organization_id
attributes.text: The id of a person's company record. Links the person to that company as a member.

attributes.name: owner
attributes.text: The current owner's name. The graph records the owner of the record.

attributes.name: owner_email
attributes.text: The current owner's email. Identifies the owner in the graph.

attributes.name: lifecycle_stage
attributes.text: The current lifecycle value.

attributes.name: person, domain, linkedin, twitter
attributes.text: The first current name, domain, LinkedIn and Twitter values, kept as their own fields as well as in the attribute lines.

attributes.name: provider_user_id
attributes.text: The Attio record id. Identifies the person in the graph, and keeps later syncs on the same document.

attributes.name: url
attributes.text: The record's address in the Attio web app. Used as the link back.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the record was created in Attio.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.record_id
attributes.text: The Attio record id. Targets one record. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.object_id
attributes.text: The Attio object id. Limits a query to one object. Not searchable.

documents.name: Deals and other object records
documents.one_document: One record of a deals object or a custom object.
documents.title: The record's name, full name, title, domain or email. Else its first filled-in attribute. Otherwise a title with the object and record id.
documents.text: A header naming the object and record, then each attribute as a labeled line, in alphabetical order. An attribute with several values shows only its first current value. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the record was created in Attio.
documents.link_back: The record in the Attio web app.

attributes.name: email, person, domain, linkedin, twitter
attributes.text: The first current email, name, domain, LinkedIn and Twitter values, kept as their own fields as well as in the attribute lines.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the record was created in Attio. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.record_id
attributes.text: The Attio record id. Targets one record. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.object_id
attributes.text: The Attio object id. Limits a query to one object. Not searchable.

attributes.name: object
attributes.text: The object's slug. Filter on it with `additional_metadata.container_id`.

documents.name: List entries
documents.one_document: One entry in one selected list: a record's place and stage values in that list.
documents.title: The list's name followed by `entry`.
documents.text: The title, then each entry attribute as a labeled line, in alphabetical order, with the first current value of each.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The record the entry is for. Links the entry to that record. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.entry_id
attributes.text: The Attio list entry id. Targets one entry. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.parent_record_id
attributes.text: The record the entry is for. Returns every list entry, note, task and comment of one record. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the entry was created. Not searchable.

attributes.name: list
attributes.text: The list's slug. Filter on it with `additional_metadata.container_id`.

documents.name: Notes
documents.title: `Comment by` and the author's name. Without an author, the first 80 characters of the text.
documents.text: The note title, then its content as markdown, or plain text when there is no markdown. Then a `Tagged` line naming the records and members tagged in it. The author, the record it is on and its creation time are part of the text too.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: Who created the note. The graph records the note as written by that person.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: Workspace members tagged in the note. Their names stay in the text, and the graph records each as mentioned. Tagged records are not included.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The record the note is on, written into the text as its id. Links the note to that record.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.note_id
attributes.text: The Attio note id. Targets one note. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.meeting_id
attributes.text: The meeting the note belongs to. Returns a meeting together with its transcript and notes. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.parent_record_id
attributes.text: The record the note is on. Returns every list entry, note, task and comment of one record. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the note was created, written as a `Created` line.

documents.name: Tasks
documents.title: The task text on one line, cut near 80 characters at a word. Otherwise a title with the task id.
documents.text: The title, the full task text when it is longer, a `Status` line with `Open` or `Completed`, the deadline and the assignees. The task's key, the record it is on and its creation time are part of the text too.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.status
attributes.text: `Open` or `Completed`, written as the `Status` line. Limits a query to open or completed tasks.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.deadline_at
attributes.text: The deadline, written as the `Deadline` line. Limits a query to a range of deadlines.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.is_completed
attributes.text: Whether the task is done. Keeps only open or only completed tasks. Not searchable.

attributes.name: Assignees
attributes.text: The people assigned to the task, written into the text. They are not attached to the task as people.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The record the task is linked to, written into the text. Places the task under that record in the graph.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.task_id
attributes.text: The Attio task id. Written into the text as part of the task's key. Targets one task.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.parent_record_id
attributes.text: The record the task is on. Returns every list entry, note, task and comment of one record. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the task was created, written as a `Created` line.

documents.name: Comments
documents.one_document: One comment on a selected record or list entry.
documents.title: `Comment by` and the author's name. Without an author, the first 80 characters of the text.
documents.text: A header naming the author and what was commented on, the id of the record or entry when there is one, then the comment text. The creation time is part of the text too.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: Who wrote the comment. The graph records the comment as written by that person.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The record or list entry the comment is on, written into the text as its id. Links the comment to it.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.thread_id
attributes.text: The discussion thread. Groups the comments of one discussion, so a reply can be read with the rest of its thread. Limits a query to one thread. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.comment_id
attributes.text: The Attio comment id. Targets one comment. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.resolved_at
attributes.text: When the comment was resolved. Finds resolved or unresolved comments. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.parent_record_id
attributes.text: The record the comment belongs to, when there is one. Returns every list entry, note, task and comment of one record. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the comment was created, written as a `Created` line.

documents.name: Meetings
documents.title: The meeting title. Otherwise a title with the meeting id.
documents.text: The title, the description, a `Starts` line and a `Participants` line.
documents.date: When the meeting was created in Attio, not when it starts.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.participants
attributes.text: The participants' names or emails, written as the `Participants` line, where HydraDB can identify the people. Filters meetings by participant.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.meeting_id
attributes.text: The Attio meeting id. Returns a meeting together with its transcript and notes. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the meeting was created in Attio. Not searchable.

documents.name: Call transcripts
documents.one_document: One call recording's transcript. A recording with no transcribed speech is skipped.
documents.title: The meeting title. Otherwise a title with the recording id.
documents.text: A header naming the call and its speakers, then the full transcript text.
documents.date: When the meeting was created in Attio.
documents.files: The audio and video recording itself is not synced. Only the transcript text is.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.speakers
attributes.text: The speakers' names, written in the header, where HydraDB can identify the people. Filters transcripts by speaker.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: The meeting the call belongs to. Links the transcript to that meeting. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.call_recording_id
attributes.text: The Attio call recording id. Targets one transcript. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.meeting_id
attributes.text: The meeting the call belongs to. Returns a meeting together with its transcript and notes. Not searchable.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: When the meeting was created in Attio. Not searchable.

example_searches: What did we discuss with Acme on our last call?
What open tasks are attached to this company?
What notes mention the pricing objection?

connections: A note or task to the record it is on.
A comment to the record or list entry it is on, and to its discussion thread.
A list entry to its record.
A call transcript to its meeting.
people: A person record stands for that person, identified by name, email and handles.
The owner of each person and company record.
The author of each note and comment, and members tagged in a note.
Task assignees, meeting participants and transcript speakers appear only in the text, where HydraDB can identify them.
graph.from_text: Record and list entry attributes, note, task and comment text, meeting participants and transcript speech.

not_synced: Records and entries from objects and lists you did not select.
Meetings outside the window, which runs from `lookback_days` ago to 30 days ahead.
Notes and tasks created before the window.
Earlier values of an attribute, and every value after the first, except emails and phones on people and companies.
Files, and the audio and video of call recordings.
